recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-33096 unless a future BR&R or terminology decision changes the THO-owned status terminology or ResearchStudy progress status model.
issue_request: FHIR-33096 is a Published/Persuasive BR&R technical correction requesting that the research-study-status code completed no longer duplicate closed-to-accrual-and-intervention, that completed mean the study closed according to plan with no further treatments, interventions, or data collection, and that the applicable binding be changed to preferred.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git commit dcb559de39164b7bc3aace21fe57cbaf57e13cc8, which changed source/researchstudy/codesystem-research-study-status.xml to the requested completed definition and changed the then-current ResearchStudy study-status binding from extensible to preferred.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread identifies the duplicated completed definition as a cut-and-paste error and explains the R5 separation between resource publication status and study progress status. Current source now has ResearchStudy.status as publication state and ResearchStudy.progressStatus.state bound to the THO research-study-status ValueSet with preferred strength. Later FHIR-50644 was resolved no-change and confirms that study lifecycle status belongs on progressStatus.state, not ResearchStudy.status.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. ResearchStudy is active in source/fhir.ini, the current code system already carries the corrected completed definition, and the active progressStatus.state binding already has preferred strength.

related_jiras.note: Resolved - No Change later issue confirms ResearchStudy.status is publication status and that ResearchStudy.progressStatus.state carries research study lifecycle status.
